---
title: 'Share builds with testers through Oore'
status: implemented
description: 'Give testers a QA Viewer account so they install the latest Android or iOS build from Oore and send feedback on it.'
---

Testers sign in to Oore on their phone, see the latest build of each app they
can access, install it, and send feedback that lands on the build. Nothing goes
through a store, so a build reaches testers as soon as it succeeds.

## Choose how testers get builds

| Delivery                                | Testers need                                | Oore needs                                        | Guide                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Google Play internal testing            | A Google account on your tester list        | Local Only is enough                              | [Deliver to testers on Google Play](/start/android/google-play)       |
| TestFlight                              | An App Store Connect user and TestFlight    | Local Only is enough                              | [Deliver to TestFlight and the App Store](/start/ios/testflight)      |
| Oore, with a tester account (this page) | An Oore sign-in; for iOS, a registered UDID | External Access; HTTPS for iOS                    | This page                                                             |
| Oore, with a share link for one file    | Only the link                               | External Access, and a developer to make the link | [Send one file without an account](#send-one-file-without-an-account) |

Use the stores when testers are outside your company or you want store review
early. Use Oore when testers are your own team and should get every build
within minutes, including Android debug builds and iOS ad hoc builds.

## What you need

- [External Access](/team/access) with OIDC or Trusted Proxy, so testers can
  sign in from their phones. For iOS installs, the address must use HTTPS.
  [How External Access works](/concepts/external-access) explains the change
  from Local Only.
- Instance owner or admin access, to invite testers, and project maintainer
  access to add them to the project.
- A pipeline that produces an installable file:
  - **Android**: any `.apk`. The `Debug APK` pipeline from
    [Build your first Android app](/start/android/first-build) works. A
    `.aab` cannot be installed from Oore.
  - **iOS**: an `.ipa` signed for **Ad hoc** distribution. An App Store IPA
    from the TestFlight path cannot be installed from Oore. Step 3 sets this
    up.

## 1. Invite each tester as a QA Viewer

1. Open **Settings > Users** and select **Invite user**.
2. Enter the tester's **Email**, exactly as your identity provider sends it.
3. For **Instance role**, choose **QA Viewer**.
4. Select **Send invite**, then send the tester the External Access address
   of Oore.

A QA Viewer can see builds, install artifacts, and send feedback in the
projects you add them to, and nothing else. See
[Invite a team member](/team/invite) for details.

## 2. Add testers to the project

1. Open the project and its **Settings** tab.
2. In the **Access** section, select **Add members**.
3. Pick the testers, or paste their emails.
4. Keep **Project role** at **Viewer**. A QA Viewer is always limited to
   Viewer.
5. Select **Add N people**.

To add testers to several projects at once, see
[Manage roles and project access](/team/roles).

## 3. Build an installable iOS version

Skip this step for Android.

An iOS build installs only on iPhones whose UDID is in its provisioning
profile. Keep the TestFlight pipeline as it is and add a second pipeline for
testers:

1. On the project's **Pipelines** tab, select **Add pipeline**, then
   **Custom**. Name it `iOS ad hoc`, and under **Platforms** select only
   **iOS**.
2. Under **Signing > iOS**, turn on **Enable iOS signing**. Choose **Ad hoc**
   for **Distribution** and **API (App Store Connect automation)** for
   **Signing mode**. Enter the same **Apple Team ID**, **Bundle identifiers**
   and **App Store Connect API key** as your TestFlight pipeline.
3. Under **Build > Artifacts**, set the pattern to `build/ios/ipa/*.ipa`.
4. Select **Create pipeline**.
5. Open the pipeline's **Edit** page. Under **Registered iOS devices**, enter
   each tester's **Device name** and **UDID**, and select **Register device**.
   Oore registers the device with Apple and syncs the profiles.
6. Run a build of the `iOS ad hoc` pipeline.

Register a device before the build that should install on it. A device
registered later needs a new build. Finding a UDID and fixing sync problems
are covered in [Register an iOS test device](/build/distribute/ios-devices).

## 4. Testers install the latest build

The tester opens the Oore address on their phone and signs in. Instead of the
operator dashboard, a QA Viewer sees **Your apps**:

1. If they can access more than one project, they pick the app at the top.
2. **Latest release** shows the newest successful build with an installable
   file, what changed, and an **Android** or **iOS** button.
3. The button opens the install page. On Android, the tester selects
   **Install**, allows the browser to install unknown apps if asked, and opens
   the APK. On an iPhone, the tester selects **Install** and confirms the iOS
   prompt.

The install page works in Safari, Chrome and other full browsers. Browsers
inside other apps, such as Gmail, can drop the iOS install link. The page then
shows a hint and a **Copy link** button to open it in a full browser.

You can also send a tester to one build directly. On the build page, open an
artifact's **Install** page and select **Copy link**. The tester still signs
in, and sees the build only if they can access the project.

Each install starts a delivery session that lasts up to one hour.
[How artifact delivery works](/concepts/artifact-delivery) explains the limits.

## 5. Testers send feedback

On **Your apps**, the tester selects **Feedback** on the latest release. They
describe **What happened?**, check the **Device**, **OS version** and **App
version** that Oore filled in, add a screenshot if it helps, and select
**Send feedback**.

The note appears on the build's timeline, with its screenshot. To get notes in
Slack, Mattermost or email as they arrive, add the **Tester feedback** event to
a channel in [Set up notifications](/team/notifications).

Screenshots can be PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 5 MiB. Each person can send up to
10 notes in 10 minutes.

## Send one file without an account

For someone who has no Oore account, such as a client checking an Android
build, a developer can create a link that works without sign-in:

1. On the build page, find the artifact and select **Share**.
2. Select **Create share link…**.
3. Choose how long it lasts under **Expires after**, from 1 hour to 7 days.
   Select **Limit to one download** if the link should work once.
4. Select **Create link**, then **Copy link**. Oore shows the link only once.

Anyone who has the link can download the file until it expires, so send it
only to the intended person. The link downloads the file. It does not install
an iOS build, so use it for APKs and other files. It uses the External Access
address, so it does not work from another device in Local Only.

**Share > Copy download link** gives a link that lasts only 15 minutes, for
quick handovers.

## Verify the result

- The tester signs in on their phone and sees **Your apps** with the project
  and its latest release.
- The app installs from the **Android** or **iOS** button and opens.
- A test note sent with **Feedback** appears on the build's timeline.

## Troubleshooting

**The tester sees "No apps shared with you yet"**

Their account is not a member of any project. Add them in the project's
**Access** section. Check that the email they sign in with matches the
invitation.

**The tester sees "No release is ready to test"**

The project has no successful build with an APK or an install-ready IPA. A
`.aab` or an App Store IPA does not count. Run a build of a pipeline that
produces one.

**iOS says the app cannot be installed**

The iPhone's UDID is not in the build's provisioning profile. Register the
device, then run a new build.

**The install page cannot be opened on the phone**

The phone cannot reach the Oore address, or it uses HTTP for an iOS install.
Check the External Access address from the phone's browser.

**The share link does not open on another device**

Oore is in Local Only, so the link points to `127.0.0.1`. Set up External
Access, then create a new link.
